summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog post introducing Mission Control, a six-month internal rotation program that lets product engineers experience Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) work.

summary.what_it_does: This is a blog post, not a software tool. It explains that Mission Control is a six-month rotation program at Google in which product-development engineers spend time on an SRE team to understand how to build and operate high-reliability services at scale. It describes the SRE definition attributed to Ben Treynor Sloss, who coined the term and started the team in 2003 with seven engineers, and says the team grew to roughly 2,000 SREs. It notes that about half of engineers who complete a rotation stay on as SREs. The author says he will rotate with the SRE team in Seattle that supports Google Compute Engine and will write follow-up posts.
notable: Mission Control is a six-month internal SRE rotation for product engineers, named after NASA's Mission Control
SREs receive jackets with a flight patch bearing the Latin motto 'Duri et Periti'

caveats: Describes an internal Google program; outside engineers cannot join the rotation
Covers only the first part of a two-part series; the page does not give the rotation's results beyond the stay-on rate
